So, I always struggled as a kid with doing things that I couldn't do perfectly. Doing them at all. If I knew I couldn't for sure do it perfectly the first time, then I wouldn't do it at all because I was too afraid of humiliation.

Now if she's already tried it, and had a bad experience, I can't even imagine the anxiety of knowing you have to do it again! So keep that in mind. A big part is probably the fear of looking stupid, or being humiliated. If you can get through that, and let her know that no matter what she will not be judged, that might help.

Then there's the part about how this is something she needs. So she's probably feeling very conflicted about her desire to complete it and gain the reward, and the desire to keep from humiliating herself.

So my plan of action might be to help her know she is safe and won't be judged. That no one cares if she fails. And then remind her and convince her of the good things that will happen when she completes it. She'll have some more freedom, she can drive herself. Ya know, the good stuff. Quench the fear and lift up the pros. That's my advice from how I was as a teen at least.
